6.text: The wife is often harshly treated by her husband. I have mentioned

7.text: the case of a husband killing his wife with a blow of a fire-brand. Blows,

8.text: though less severe, are not infrequently dealt out to women; but it also

9.text: happens that a wife ill-treats her husband. I recall one man of small stature,

10.text: with but little physical strength, but very irascible. Quarrels between him

11.text: and his wife were not rare. When it would come to blows, his wife would

12.text: throw him, and keep him down, asking, “Have you enough? Will you cease?”

13.text: until he would say, “Enough, I will cease.” His neighbors told me this story

22.text: the people went to attend the funeral, the women who assisted in dressing

23.text: the body in his funeral clothes saw with surprise that the wound was on the

26.text: confirmed the story that their father was killed by his own request. He had

27.text: no near relatives in the country, and the murder was allowed to go without

28.text: any attempt at blood-vengeance. The woman took the herd and remained

29.text: its possessor. In the course of time she took another husband, who lived on

30.text: her herd, and was therefore wholly dependent on her.

31.text: The position of old women, however, is much inferior to that of old men.

32.text: Among the Reindeer Chukchee a widow having children may remain the

33.text: owner of the herd, and keep that position till her children are grown up.

34.text: Among the Maritime Chukchee an old widow lives with one of her sons; and

35.text: her voice is of no great influence, even among the occupants of the inner

36.text: sleeping-room, unless she happens to be a shaman or a “knowing one.”¹
36.note: Footnote marker at 4x is a raised digit set clearly above the baseline, keyed as superscript U+00B9 per §2.10, not the ASCII digit the draft carried.

37.text: The inferior position of the woman does not exclude tender love between

38.text: husband and wife. Especially do marriages contracted among children develop

39.text: into a very strong tie between the married couples. When I travelled on

40.text: the Wolverene River, an epidemic of influenza appeared among the Chukchee.
